US Electricity Dashboard

Utility costs, rates, and customers — state and utility level. Data: EIA 861 & FERC Form 1. All dollars inflation-adjusted to 2024 (CPI-U).

Investor-owned utilities serve ~70% of US customers. Capital spending has tripled since 2001 to $118B/year — distribution ($52B), transmission ($28B), and renewables+storage ($13B) lead growth.

State rate trends
Each dot = one utility (500+ GWh/yr, 87% of US electricity). Rates now combine bundled + delivery service types, correcting for CCA restructuring in CA, OH, MA, etc.
Pattern: IOUs (red) averaged real rate increases. Cooperatives (green) and municipals (blue) got cheaper on average. Purple dots = Community Choice Aggregators.
Residential customers grow ~1%/yr. Industrial sales show interesting load growth patterns from data centers and electrification.
Industrial sales growth — where the load is going
Utilities in Louisiana, New Mexico, Iowa, Oregon, North Dakota lead — consistent with data center corridors.
